agree.reason: The candid tone and clear budget would reassure a wary backer, but the pitch leaves out the refund guarantee, the two-week update promise, the reviewer video and even the game's name, which are the things most likely to win over someone who has already lost $85.

honest.reason: It drops 'proven hit' and frames the 23 convention-heavy ratings fairly, though 'shipping outside the US isn't priced yet' is an unsupplied claim and 'three years' rounds up a little.

works_the_facts.reason: The budget arithmetic is correct and useful (572 backers, about $25,350 in costs, about $2,700 headroom), but it never notes that 572 backers is only 46% of the 1,240 sign-ups, which is the most favourable true figure available.

right_comparison.reason: The only alternative it gives is the bare line 'this campaign is how the game gets made', with nothing on what happens to backers or the game if the goal is missed.

qualification.reason: November 2027 is stated as an estimate with nothing attached if it slips, even though the writer could have named the full refund for deliveries more than three months late.

objections.reason: It deals directly with the first-time-creator worry (finished design and art, signed quote, itemised costs), but it leaves out the refund and update commitments that answer the fear of non-delivery, and it ends the ratings section on self-doubt.

fit.reason: It is about 500 words and laid out as a crowdfunding pitch, but it never names the game or the creator, which a campaign page needs.
